meaning.zh:
“祝好运” 或 “加油”。

这个惯用语起源于戏剧和表演艺术界。通常，在演员上场前，其他演员会祝他 “摔断腿”（Break a leg），听似不吉利，但实际上是为了避开坏运（因为直接祝 “好运” 被认为会带来厄运）。如今，这个短语已经被广泛用于各种场合，表示希望对方在某个活动或任务中取得成功。
meaning.en: This idiom originates from the theater and performing arts. Traditionally, instead of saying "good luck," which is considered bad luck, actors would tell each other to "break a leg" before a performance. Today, it’s widely used in various contexts to wish someone success.

lines.en: You're going to do great in your performance tonight. *Break a leg*!
lines.zh: 你今晚的表演一定会很棒。加油！

lines.en: Before her big presentation, her colleague told her, "*Break a leg*."
lines.zh: 在她的重要演讲前，她的同事对她说：“祝好运。”

lines.en: As he went on stage, his friends shouted, "*Break a leg*!"
lines.zh: 当他上台的时候，他的朋友们大声喊道：“加油！”
